response.answer: We will use a participatory workshop methodology to convert qualitative acceptability into numeric fairness thresholds, simulate harms, and set stop/go criteria. This approach involves stakeholder engagement and quantitative analysis.

results.title: Perspective Chapter: UNFC and UNRMS – Global Tools Enabling ...
results.content: UNRMS aims to be the connector between a project-based classification using UNFC and a holistic management system grounded in the elements of the SDGs. Based on 12 fundamental principles and a set of requirements, UNRMS guides governments, companies, and financiers through the full resource life cycle—exploration, development, production, reuse, and closure—so that every decision can be tested against technical, social, environmental, and economic performance criteria drawn from the 2030 Agenda [41]. UNFC structures data and information to classify a resource project according to three main categories: the Environmental-Socio-Economic Viability (E Category), the Technical Feasibility (F Category), and the Degree of Confidence in the estimated quantities of potential production (G Category). UNRMS principles and requirements for responsible management of resources, coupled with UNFC classifications of actual and potential projects and production, provide a powerful approach to addressing the challenge of sustainable resource management.

results.title: Florida Statute § 1006 - Online Sunshine
results.content: 1006.062 Administration of medication and provision of medical services by district school board personnel.— (1) Notwithstanding the provisions of the Nurse Practice Act, part I of chapter 464, district school board personnel may assist students in the administration of prescription medication when the following conditions have been met: (a) Each district school board shall include in its approved school health services plan a procedure to provide training, by a registered nurse, a licensed practical nurse, or an advanced practice registered nurse licensed under chapter 464 or by a physician licensed under chapter 458 or chapter 459, or a physician assistant licensed under chapter 458 or chapter 459, to the school personnel designated by the school principal to assist students in the administration of prescribed medication. (4) EMERGENCY DRILLS; EMERGENCY PROCEDURES.— (a) Formulate and prescribe policies and procedures, in consultation with the appropriate public safety agencies, for emergency drills and for actual emergencies, including, but not limited to, fires, natural disasters, active assailant and hostage situations, and bomb threats, for all students and faculty at all public schools of the district composed of grades K-12, pursuant to State Board of Education rules.
